errors.quote: Select the lowest intensity/duration that produces a reproducible dissociation.
errors.issue: The proposed dissociation is the desired behavioral result. Tuning the intervention until that pattern appears does not independently validate inhibition and can favor a false positive. Calibrate terminal transmission and kinetics independently, then freeze the manipulation.

errors.quote: This is optional but strengthens inference.
errors.issue: The independent neural efficacy check is made optional. Histology plus a behavior-selected light dose cannot establish the intended loss of P-to-Q output or interpret a null; functional validation belongs in core acceptance criteria.

errors.quote: light begins at cue onset and ends at response commitment, go signal, or the pre-registered end of the retrieval epoch.
errors.issue: No explicit suppression-offset/rebound measurement or recovery-before-go criterion accompanies this rule. The intervention can persist into movement despite optical epoch separation.

errors.quote: Confirm that cue detection is intact by ensuring animals respond to both cue types at comparable baseline rates.
errors.issue: Baseline performance does not exclude an inhibition-induced sensory deficit. The final rule invokes cue-detection controls, but an operational same-cue sensory task under the active manipulation is missing.

errors.quote: Analyze trials where movement initiation occurs within the normal baseline range. If the choice deficit persists, retrieval impairment is more plausible.
errors.issue: This selects on a treatment-affected outcome and can distort the comparison. The earlier mediator caveat helps, but this troubleshooting rule still treats selection as affirmative causal evidence.

rationale: Correct terminal targeting, broad controls and an explicit warning about post-treatment adjustment. However, behavioral tuning replaces mandatory independent suppression validation, recovery timing and active sensory controls remain incomplete, and repeated text obscures the decisive gaps. Requires substantive revisions before use.
reference_guardrails: O1 establishes that population P has two targets, not that every Q-projecting neuron collateralizes. Do not assume either overlap or disjointness; validate or retain the limitation.

Projection-defined somatic inhibition tests a population and all its affected outputs. Local Q-terminal intervention is preferable for a pathway claim but also needs actual transmission and off-target validation.
Suppression in neuronal somata does not guarantee suppression of terminal transmission. Validate physiological onset, sustained effect, offset recovery and rebound at the actual behavioral settings.

Reduced normal performance supports a conditional causal requirement, not memory storage or an exclusive retrieval computation. Cue perception, attention, maintenance and motor preparation remain alternatives.
Light offset is not necessarily inhibition offset. A choice made after light ends can correctly report an earlier retrieval deficit; outcome timing alone is not a rebound diagnosis.
Movement adjustment/matching after intervention and conditioning on response completion can bias inference. Report all randomized trials and use experimental motor/sensory dissociations.
A nonsignificant control effect is not equivalence. Predefine biologically meaningful bounds and obtain enough precision to exclude consequential confounds.
Two pathways or epochs can both be necessary. Effects in an other-projection control do not by themselves invalidate the tested pathway contribution.

Numbers missing from the packet may be proposed as pilot settings; no specific opsin, surgical coordinate or animal count is mandatory. Operational calibration and justified independent-animal sampling are required.

Reference correction: population-level divergence must not be described as demonstrated single-neuron collateralization. Terminal effects on intended local Q signaling are part of the intervention, not automatically an off-target artifact.
